title: Small decision-tree depth yields narrow DNF and CNF
statement: Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $d$ be a natural number such that the decision-tree depth of $f$ is at most $d$. Then $f$ is computed by a DNF formula of width at most $d$ and by a CNF formula of width at most $d$; that is, there exist a disjunction of terms and a conjunction of clauses, each term or clause containing at most $d$ literals, that both agree with $f$ on every input.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
decision-tree depth of f is at most d
replaced:
If $\mathrm{dtDepth}\,f \leq d$, then $f$ is computed by a DNF of width at most
$d$ and by a CNF of width at most $d$.
